title: Operator pocket guide: observability heuristics and sparse metrics
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused cheat sheet for building and maintaining inference observability with an emphasis on small, high-signal metrics ("sparse metrics"), trace annotation guidance, and dashboard heuristics that minimize query cost. Intended for on-call, SREs, and engineers who ship quick dashboards or triage playbooks.

Why sparse metrics?
- Token-serving systems are high-cardinality and high-volume. Full telemetry at token-level is prohibitively expensive.
- Sparse metrics = a curated set of low-cardinality counters/gauges plus sampled traces and event markers that answer 80% of operational questions.
- Goal: fast root-cause with <2 queries and <30s time-to-first-insight.

Core SLI candidates (compact, actionable):
- request.latency.p50_ms (unit: ms) -- compute at edge/ingest with P50/P95/P99 rollups.
- request.success_rate (unit: fraction) -- 1 - error_rate where error includes 5xx, model-fallback, truncated responses.
- tokens.cost_per_1000 (unit: USD per 1k tokens) -- derived in billing pipeline (daily). Useful for regression alerts.
- model.fallback_rate (unit: fraction) -- fraction of requests routed to fallback variant.
- kvcache.hit_ratio (unit: fraction) -- prefix/KV cache effectiveness aggregated per route.
- batch.size_avg (unit: items) -- average batch size over 1m window. Indicates throughput behavior.
- queue.time_ms.p95 (unit: ms) -- time spent waiting before execution; early indicator of saturation.

Metric naming heuristics (keep short, predictable):
- dot-delimited, lower_snake_case for segments. Prefix by domain: request., model., infra., billing., cache.
- include unit in dashboards, not in the metric name.
- avoid per-model explosion unless critical; use tags for model/version when needed (see sampling rules).

Tagging and cardinality policy:
- Allowed tags: region, route, customer_tier (free|paid|enterprise), model_family (small set), request_type (generation|embed|rerank).
- Disallowed as primary tags: tenant_id, user_id, exact_prompt_hash. Those should only appear in sampled traces/events.
- If you need per-model metrics for a rollout, create a temporary metric with TTL and a TODO to delete after 90 days.

Trace annotation conventions (for tokenized inference):
- Span root: request:{request_id} with set tags: route, model_family, region, customer_tier, request_type.
- Annotate important events as span logs: kvcache.lookup (bool), batch_start, batch_end, model_call.start, model_call.end, fallback_switch.
- Add a short field "tokens_consumed" to the root span (integer) for cost attribution in traces. Do NOT log full prompts.
- Keep trace payloads minimal: include only identifiers and short strings (<512B) and avoid PII.
- Sampling policy: deterministic 1/1000 sampling for cold traces + adaptive 100% sampling for traces with error or >p99 latency.

Dashboard composition heuristics (one-pagers, 4–6 panels):
- Top row: health indicators (requests/s, error rate, p95 latency) and SLI status.
- Mid row: resource signals (GPU utilization of pools, queue time p95, batch size avg).
- Bottom row: cost & rollout signals (tokens.cost_per_1000 trend, fallback_rate, model_version breakdown for active rollouts).
- Small multipliers: quick links to the most recent sampled trace for a given route (trace id link).

Query-cost conscious visualization tips:
- Use pre-aggregated rollups (1m/5m) for long windows. Real-time exploration can use live summarization with limited time span (last 15m).
- Prefer timeseries with stat functions stored server-side (p95 from histogram buckets) rather than on-the-fly percentile calculations.
- Avoid high-cardinality group-bys on dashboard defaults. Provide a drilldown panel that runs more expensive queries only when a user clicks.

Alerting checklist (actionable, rate-limited):
- Alert 1: SLI degradation (request.success_rate < 99% for 5m AND increase relative to baseline > 50% ) -> P1 oncall.
- Alert 2: Latency shift (request.latency.p95 increased by >40% over 30m, absolute > 1200ms) -> investigate batching/queue.
- Alert 3: Queue growth (queue.time_ms.p95 > 1500ms and queue.depth increasing) -> scale or throttle.
- Alert 4: Cost spike (tokens.cost_per_1000 over rolling 1h > baseline*2) -> runway check + throttle policy.
- All alerts should attach the last 3 trace ids sampled for that route and a quick note of recent deploys.

Runbook snippets (triage flow):
1) Check SLI dashboards. Identify which dimension (route, region, model_family) shows delta.
2) Open latest sampled traces for that dimension. Look at kvcache lookup, batch_start/end, and model_call durations.
3) If batch sizes collapsed to 1 or queue time spiked, suspect autoscaler/worker preemption or routing change.
4) Check recent deploys (github/ci link in dashboard) and canary traffic split.
5) Mitigation: roll back canary, increase worker pool, enable throttling, or route to fallback variant. Always document mitigation in ticket.

Maintenance & hygiene rules:
- Metrics lifecycle: every metric must have an owner in metric-catalog. Unowned metrics older than 180 days get archived.
- Dashboard reviews: lightweight quarterly review. Remove expensive panels or set them to be on-demand.
- Rollouts: enable high-fidelity sampling (1% full traces) for the first 48 hours of a model version, then decay to standard sampling.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define exact thresholds for cost spike alerts per customer_tier (JIRA:OBS-3421).
- Prototype a lightweight trace-index that can be queried by token-range without exposing prompt text.
- Add a compact panel showing three example high-latency traces with annotated span durations.

Quick links and references:
- metric catalog: confluence:metrics-catalog (internal)
- rollout policy doc: confluence:rollouts
- ticket for sampling infra: JIRA:OBS-3421
- telemetry PRs: github:telemetry/ship#987

Notes to self / informal: 
- Keep this doc slim — intended to be printed as a 1-pager.
- When in doubt, prefer fewer metrics + good traces over very wide metric coverage.
- If we hit alert noise, add a severity dampener rather than removing signal outright.
